newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Inmates free final hostages from Colombian prison.
newsitem.headline: Inmates free final hostages from Colombian prison.

text.p: Rebellious inmates released 11 hostages from a prison in northern Colombia on Sunday, more than a week after killing three guards and a policeman in a bloody takeover of the penitentiary, authorities said.

Police and penal authorities said the hostages, the last being held inside the jail, were released shortly after 2 p.m. local time (1900 GMT) as part of an agreement between government officials and inmates aimed at ending a 10-day-old uprising.
The hostages, six men and five women, including the prison's deputy director, were all said to be in relatively good health although two were suffering from hypertension.

Five other hostages had been freed since a group of about 10 heavily armed inmates seized control of the ageing, chronically overcrowded jail in Valledupar, capital of northern Cesar province, on April 3.

Jose Noe Rios, Colombia's deputy labour minister and chief government negotiator with the rebellious prisoners, said they had agreed to lay down their arms on Monday as part of the negotiated settlement of the uprising that was brokered by members of the International Committee of the Red Cross.

In exchange, Noe Rios said the government agreed to take no reprisals against leaders of the rebellion and to move quickly to improve living conditions inside the Valledupar facility, which was built to house no more than 150 inmates but currently holds more than 580. The government also agreed to ensure that the legal cases of the rebel inmates will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis.

Tension flared on Wednesday when authorities discovered a tunnel the inmates were apparently planning to use in a mass escape attempt. It erupted anew early on Sunday, when inmates engaged in a brief firefight with police surrounding the compound. No one was hurt in the 15-minute shootout, which was apparently triggered by fears that authorities were preparing to retake the prison by force.
Leaders of the takeover, all hardened criminals, initially demanded helicopters and bulletproof vests for a ride to freedom and possible exile in Cuba.
In addition to improved living conditions they also demanded freedom for a select group of prisoners.
